title: Everything Passes
description: Twelve minutes watching sounds, sensations and thoughts arise and pass, until impermanence stops being an idea.

segments.say: Sit comfortably, and let your eyes close.
Take a few slightly deeper breaths, then let the breath go on by itself.
Today we will look at something simple, which the Buddha put at the centre of everything: nothing that appears stays.
You already know this as an idea. Now we will watch it happen.
Start with sounds. Let your ears open, without looking for anything.
Notice that every sound begins, lasts a little, and ends.
It does not matter what the sound is. Just notice the beginning and the end.
Even the silence between sounds changes.
Now bring your attention to the body. To your hands.
What looks like a still hand is, up close, movement. Tingling, warmth, pulsing.
Pick one sensation and follow it. How long does it stay the same?
Notice that even the most solid sensation is not one thing. It is made of small moments, one after another.
Now the breath.
Each breath is new. This one has never happened before, and will not happen again.
Feel the end of the out-breath. The small space before the next one.
Last, thoughts.
You do not need to stop thinking. Just notice when a thought appears.
And notice that it leaves too. Sometimes in the middle of a sentence.
No thought has stayed so far. Not even the ones that felt urgent.
When we stop expecting things to stay, there is less to hold on to.
That is true of the good things, the ones we want to keep.
And it is true of the hard things, the ones that feel like they will never pass.
Stay a little longer with whatever is happening now, knowing it is already changing.
This practice is ending too. Let it end.
When you are ready, open your eyes.
